name: 1 Mile North
label: Ba Da Bing!
lede: Jon Hills made the first 1 Mile North album with the natural reverb of the dilapidated Brooklyn sweater factory he lived in. The second got a 9.0 from Pitchfork; then came ten years off and three more albums, made on his own.

hero.by: Photos from the Minor Shadows sessions, c. 2003, inside the 2015 vinyl reissue

eras.title: Reverb from a sweater factory
eras.text: After The Capital Suite, Jon Hills recorded sketches and live takes in a Brooklyn apartment from 1998 on. Mutual Skies later placed the project's start in the wave of post-rock and ambient guitar "typified by Kranky acts." The first album came out on Old Colony Recordings, which had released the Capital Suite record.

years.src: Deathwish: Glass Wars · Shallow Rewards: 1 Mile North, Minor Shadows
years.h: Hills starts recording sketches in a Brooklyn apartment
years.p: The sketches and live recordings Jon Hills made there from 1998 to 2002 later fill a bonus side of the Glass Wars vinyl, including Altare della Patria and Force Feeder.
years.xp: Pitchfork's review of the second album said Glass Wars got its natural reverb from "the dilapidated Brooklyn sweater factory Hills called home in the late '90s."

years.cap: Photos from the Glass Wars recording period, c. 2001, inside the 2015 vinyl reissue
years.src: Discogs: 1 Mile North, Glass Wars · AllMusic: Glass Wars · Mutual Skies: 1 Mile North, The Sunken Nest · Discogs: Old Colony Recordings
years.h: Old Colony follows the Capital Suite with Glass Wars
years.p: Seven tracks, catalog COL002, with Escorting Deep Waters past eleven minutes. Hills plays strings, keyboards and sampler and records it; Mark Bajuk adds keyboards and field recordings.
years.xp:
AllMusic's James Mason called it "a quiet masterpiece." It was re-released on September 30, 2003.

Mutual Skies, the Cape Cod label Discogs says Old Colony now trades as, wrote in 2022 of 1 Mile North, "whose debut album Glass Wars we released over twenty years ago (as Old Colony Recordings)."

years.h: Sketches from Back Then, a digital EP
years.p: Streaming services date the 1 Mile North EP to 2002. Wikipedia lists a Wortcunner edition in 2016.

eras.title: Ba Da Bing! and a 9.0
eras.text: Brooklyn's Ba Da Bing! took the second album, and a Pitchfork review gave Minor Shadows a 9.0. In 2004 came concert recordings and a three-way split CD with Colophon, the solo project of Tarentel's Jefre Cantu-Ledesma.

years.cap: Contact sheets from the Minor Shadows sessions, c. 2003, inside the 2015 vinyl reissue
years.src: Ba Da Bing!: 1 Mile North · Discogs: 1 Mile North, Minor Shadows · Shallow Rewards: 1 Mile North, Minor Shadows
yt: In 1983 He Loved to Fly, from Minor Shadows
years.p: Seven tracks, from Jamie Wagner's trumpet on In 1983 He Loved To Fly to the 13-minute The Manual. Bajuk is credited with analog keyboards.
years.xp:
The label's bio said Hills took from Vini Reilly of the Durutti Column the knack of shaping "subtle melodies out of abstract structures." Bajuk, it said, "by day designs 3-D imaging for the Hayden Planetarium," a classically trained pianist with a collection of analog synthesizers.

The Pitchfork review heard dialogue sampled from the 1984 documentary Streetwise on In 1983 He Loved To Fly and from Nil By Mouth on Black Lines.

q: There's a genuine soul residing in this music.
years.src: Shallow Rewards: 1 Mile North, Minor Shadows · Album of the Year: Pitchfork 2003 · AllMusic: Minor Shadows · Opus: Minor Shadows
years.p: The review compares it to the Durutti Column's Without Mercy and Eno's Discreet Music.
years.xp: Album of the Year's aggregate puts it 14th among Pitchfork's highest-scored records of 2003. AllMusic's Mark Pytlik called it "a slow and meditative record that requires time to germinate."

years.h: Altare Della Patria collects home and concert recordings, 2000 to 2003
years.p: Wikipedia lists the home and concert recordings on Old Colony. They're most of what the public record has of 1 Mile North live: no venues, dates or bills have surfaced.

years.h: A three-way split with Colophon and the Wind-Up Bird
years.p: Part three of the Music Fellowship's Triptych series puts East Coast Harbor, Ashes & Dust and Silence The Deaf beside Colophon, the solo project of Tarentel's Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, who also designed it.

eras.title: Ten years off, and the music goes to the movies
eras.text: Then nothing new for a decade; the band's site calls it an unofficial break "that ended up lasting 10 goddamn years." Mutual Skies says life and responsibilities intruded. The old records kept working, in documentaries.

years.h: Evil Architecture turns up in the Oscar-nominated Facing Fear
years.p: Jason Cohen's short documentary credits the Glass Wars track to Jonathan Hills and Mark Bajuk. Wikipedia also names two Steven Okazaki films that used the band's music, White Light/Black Rain and The Conscience of Nhem En.
Jon Hills posts a video teaser on Facebook, the earliest sign found that 1 Mile North's long break is ending.

eras.title: Back on 180-gram vinyl
eras.text: Wortcunner, a vinyl side label of Robotic Empire, reissued both early albums and then put out the first new 1 Mile North album since 2003. From here on the credits are Hills' alone.

years.src: Drowned in Sound: Wortcunner announcement · Deathwish: Glass Wars · Deathwish: Minor Shadows
yt: Force Feeder (live), from the Glass Wars reissue
years.h: Glass Wars and Minor Shadows return as 300-copy double LPs
years.p: James Plotkin remasters both for Wortcunner, on clear and white vinyl, each with a bonus side: the 1998 to 2002 sketches on one, the 2004 split tracks on the other.
years.xp: Robotic Empire announced them on the Drowned in Sound forum on October 16, calling Wortcunner "a new vinyl label initiated by Lindsay (manager of Robotic Empire Records)."

years.src: Deathwish: Awakened by Decay · 1 Mile North (northernmile.com) · A Strangely Isolated Place · SoundCloud: Mysteries of the Deep
yt: Underground Waves, from Awakened by Decay
years.h: [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] masters Awakened by Decay, two years in the making
years.p: Seven tracks recorded in Brooklyn, the last, Beyond Darkness, past sixteen minutes; 300 copies on 180-gram vinyl. The band's site calls it "a soundtrack for the void beyond the darkness."
years.xp:
Hills on Facebook: "FINALLY, the new 1 Mile North album is done and pressed to 180g wax!"

A Strangely Isolated Place recommended it to anyone who leans "into the post-rock side of ambient music," and in April 2017 put Broken Corners in its Mysteries of the Deep mix.

eras.title: A lockdown album from Fire Island
eras.text: Wortcunner put out a digital-only album in February 2020. The fifth, written in isolation during lockdown, came out on Mutual Skies, the Cape Cod label Discogs says Old Colony now trades as.

years.src: Robotic Empire: Tombs & Cocoons · Destroy//Exist: Drying the Fuse · acidted: Ambient Sunday
years.p: Eight tracks on Wortcunner, with a cover by Eric Ogden, closing on Deja Vu With Pajo.
years.xp: Destroy//Exist heard it as "firmly post rock in essence," with glimpses of drone and Americana. The Ambient Sunday blog was surprised by the trumpets and brass: "Utterly beguiling."

years.cap: Guitars and an axe in a wood-panelled room, the picture on 1 Mile North's home page
years.src: Mutual Skies: 1 Mile North, The Sunken Nest · Post-Punk.com: The Sunken Nest
years.h: Hills writes The Sunken Nest alone on Fire Island
years.p: Mutual Skies says Jon Hills wrote and recorded the album in isolation on Fire Island during lockdown. Its subject, as he described it to Post-Punk.com, is the sea.
years.xp: Post-Punk.com listed Morricone, Eno, Philip Glass, Mogwai and Earth as touchstones. Mutual Skies called it "as redolent of his teenage years in the Boston hardcore scene" as of midlife.

yt: Find Rest, from The Sunken Nest
years.h: Find Rest goes up on Hills' own YouTube channel
years.p: The first single from The Sunken Nest, posted by Jon Hills a few weeks before the CD.

years.cap: A stack of The Sunken Nest CDs
years.src: Discogs: 1 Mile North, The Sunken Nest
years.h: Mutual Skies releases The Sunken Nest, the fifth album
years.p: Catalog MSKS006, on CD and then streaming: seven tracks, mixed by Sonny DiPerri and mastered by Kramer, from Plunge Forth to Your Sunken Nest.

years.cap: Hills' music room, from 1 Mile North's Bandcamp page
years.p: Dreams Without Meaning and Cellar Bound (November 27) come out under 1 Mile North. Hills' Instagram says the October track had already slipped onto an A Cheery Wave Records compilation.

years.src: Instagram: 1 Mile North, Mar 13, 2024 · Skidmore News, Apr 6, 1995 · Discogs: Mutual Skies
years.h: Hills tracks down Stillmotion's lost masters
years.p: On 1 Mile North's Instagram, Jon Hills says he first saw Stillmotion in '93 at TT's in Boston. He tracked down the band's lost sessions and had Kramer remaster them 30 years later. Mutual Skies put the remastered sessions out as Stillmotion's 1992-1995.
years.xp: Hills: "Their music and friendship were massively special to me." Stillmotion had shared a Falstaff's bill with Hills' college band [[Creepy Woods|ms-creepy-woods]] in March 1995.
